# Identification Phase 3: portal-facing flows on the generation kit

**Generated by `npm run idphase3` from `scripts/build-identification-phase3.mjs`. Do not edit by hand.**

[IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md](../../../reference/identification/IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md) §13, Phase 3. Each file is
the flow's root scope, built from the conformance stage (`scripts/build-identification-conformance.mjs`, built in
memory and not kept as packages) or, for IP_SCAN_INTAKE, which that stage does not cover, from the tenant capture,
with the Phase 3 edits below applied. IP_SCAN_INTAKE's root scope sets the variables its flow
declares above it; keep those **Initialize variable** steps when pasting it.
`tests/identification-phase3.test.mjs` runs every file in the strict simulator (`scripts/lib/wdl-sim.mjs`)
against an in-memory SharePoint that keeps the lists' columns and the counter's ETag rule.

## Before pasting

- Phase 1 is complete: the identity columns exist on Portal Registry, Portal Status Timeline and Portal Flow
  Telemetry, and Flow Configuration holds `ENVIRONMENT_CODE` (`prd`) and the `DATASET_*` rows
  ([provisioning](../../../reference/identification/provisioning/README.md)).
- Phase 2 is complete: the kit's claim passed the tenant exit test
  ([identification-phase2](../identification-phase2/README.md)).
- **One list setting, once.** The VOID row (owner decision Q2) writes Status `void`, which is not among Portal
  Registry's Status choices (`portal-field-spec.json`: received, validation, review, action-required, approved,
  declined, withdrawn). NEDMS → Portal Registry → *List settings* → **Status** → add the choice `void` → OK.
  Nothing else changes; the existing choices and the default stay as they are.
- **One value to confirm, for SUPPORT.** In Flow Configuration, `DATASET_RECORD_LINKS_LIST_ID` must hold
  `c3875803-8a9c-42d6-86b9-85e3f0ca5eef`, the DGO_RecordLinks list ID the Phase 1 completion run recorded. The
  provisioning template shipped it as "(set after the list is created)". If it still says that, the ABOUT link is
  not written (the case itself is unaffected).

## How to apply

**All at once:** `npm run flows:update -- apply` writes every package below into its flow, backing each flow up first and
reading it back ([FLOWS_UPDATE.md](../../deployment/FLOWS_UPDATE.md)). Or by hand, one flow at a time:

For each flow: open it, delete the root scope named below, select the step above where it was, choose
**Paste an action**, paste the file, and save. If a step shows *Invalid connection*, open it, choose the existing
SharePoint connection once, and the others pick it up. Then run the flow's test.

## Changes

### CG_Submission_Endpoint

Source: the conformance stage, built in memory by `scripts/build-identification-conformance.mjs` (`SUBMISSION__CG_Submission_Endpoint__de9ef13b.paste.json`).

- The proof check is safe when no proof is sent. The portal's first call never carries one, so the proof lookup is skipped and its value is null; first() of null fails the step, which the live flow escapes only if the service stops evaluating and() at its first false argument. It now reads first() of an empty list instead.
- B5 / §8.3: duplicate check by query, then comparison. The register is queried for the same sender, subject and attachment count in the last 24 hours (indexed columns, as before), and each row found is compared on EventDate and AttachmentHashSet: the first 12 hex characters of each declared SHA-256, compared as a set (union sizes), so the order the files were declared in does not matter. The client localId is no longer read (§8.1, V9), and LocalId is no longer written (§10.2: retired).
- §8.2: the Registry Reference is claimed by the generation kit (10 flat attempts with a 1 to 5 s Delay, HTTP MERGE with IF-MATCH, the counter row found by Prefix and Year and created by the first claim of a year), as proven by the Phase 2 exit run. The flow's own three attempts are removed. The kit reads the counter and register addresses from Flow Configuration (DATASET_SEQUENCE_COUNTERS_*, DATASET_INTAKE_REGISTER_*) and the environment prefix from ENVIRONMENT_CODE (prd: none). The claim never issues at or below the highest NITDA-<year> number already in Portal Registry (the kit floor read): a counter row that is missing or behind the register can no longer reissue a reference in use, as it did live on 5 October 2026 (NITDA-2026-00001 refused as a duplicate Reference ID).
- §10.2 / §6.5: the register row carries its Entity Key, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, Direction In, AttachmentHashSet, and the Request ID as both CorrelationId (this flow starts the transaction) and CreatedByRequest.
- §8.2 / B8: if the record write fails after the claim, a VOID row accounts for the number (Title VOID, ReferenceId, Status void, SenderEmail, IdState VOID, VoidReason RECORD_WRITE_FAILED: owner decision Q2). The run still ends in the 500 path.
- §10.2 STATUS_TIMELINE: the RECEIVED event carries its own Entity Key, SubjectKey and RootKey (REC:<key>), RootRef, Action RECEIVED, RequestId, CorrelationId, RevAfter 1, Process INTAKE and ContractKey SUBMISSION.
- §8.3: every reply carries requestId, the flow's own guid().
- §10.2 FLOW_TELEMETRY: the run row carries RequestId, CorrelationId, ClientCorrelationId and the Flow Registry Key DGO:<flow ID>, and ContractKey SUBMISSION.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Registry_Alert_Email, Send_Sender_Acknowledgement_Email, Send_Rate_Limit_Alert_Email, Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

### CG_Portal_Support_Endpoint

Source: the conformance stage, built in memory by `scripts/build-identification-conformance.mjs` (`SUPPORT__CG_Portal_Support_Endpoint__4873c936.paste.json`).

- Send_Helpdesk_Alert_Email: the citizen's address is its Reply-To only when well formed; otherwise the registry's reply address (a malformed address made Outlook refuse the alert, tenant 2026-10-18).
- §8.3: the live draw (five CASE-XXXXXX candidates checked in one query, the first unused one taken) already meets the case reference rule and is kept. When all five collide, the flow now answers 503 RETRY_LATER and writes nothing; before, it wrote the fifth candidate, a duplicate. The replay branch it replaces was unreachable: no client reference is accepted (§8.1).
- A repeat of the same case is answered with the case already opened, not a second one: a case from the same e-mail address with the same topic and message in the last hour returns its reference (replayed: true), writes nothing and sends no e-mail. On 5 October 2026 the endpoint ran 24 times in one minute for one case from one phone (the portal outbox resending it; fixed in document-portal/js/core.js), and a browser that gives up on a slow run resends a case the flow did create. Portal Support Cases holds under a hundred rows, so the address and time filter is safe without an index; the message, a Note column, is compared in the flow. A failed lookup counts as no repeat.
- §10.2 SUPPORT_CASES: the case row carries its Entity Key, CaseRef, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, and the Request ID as CorrelationId and CreatedByRequest.
- §6.4 / T5: when the request names a reference, the flow finds that record by exact ReferenceId (V10) and, if the record has an Entity Key, writes an ABOUT link CAS → REC to Record Links (LinkMatchKey = FromKey|ABOUT|ToKey), addressed through Flow Configuration (DATASET_RECORD_LINKS_*). A record written before Phase 3 has no Entity Key until the Phase 5 backfill; it keeps the free-text AboutReference only. A failed link never fails the case: the reply follows the link step whatever its outcome.
- §8.3: every reply carries requestId, the flow's own guid().
- §10.2 FLOW_TELEMETRY: the run row carries RequestId, CorrelationId, ClientCorrelationId and the Flow Registry Key DGO:<flow ID>, and ContractKey SUPPORT.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Helpdesk_Alert_Email, Send_Support_Acknowledgement_Email, Send_Rate_Limit_Alert_Email, Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

Steps added: `Condition_Support_Collision`, `Condition_Support_Repeat`, `Compose_Result_Support_200_Repeat`, `Compose_Result_Support_503`, `Compose_EntityKey_Case`, `Scope_About_Link`, `Condition_About_Given`, `Get_About_Record`, `Condition_About_Has_Key`, `Get_Dataset_Bindings`, `Select_Dataset_Bindings`, `Compose_Dataset_Bindings`, `Compose_About_Link`, `Create_About_Link`, `Get_Recent_Support_Cases`, `Select_Support_Repeat`, `Compose_Support_Repeat_Ref`, `Compose_Support_Acknowledgement_Html_Part3`, `Create_Send_Support_Acknowledgement_Email_Receipt`, `Compose_Send_Support_Acknowledgement_Email_Outcome`, `Compose_Helpdesk_Alert_Html_Part3`, `Create_Send_Helpdesk_Alert_Email_Receipt`, `Compose_Send_Helpdesk_Alert_Email_Outcome`, `Create_Send_Rate_Limit_Alert_Email_Receipt`, `Compose_Send_Rate_Limit_Alert_Email_Outcome`, `Create_Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email_Receipt`, `Compose_Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email_Outcome`.

The Entity Key begins with the 8 hex characters SUBMISSION put in the stored file name, so the name carries the first 8 hex of the attachment's key as §8.3 requires; a ticket from before Phase 3 gets a fresh guid(). A record written before Phase 3 has no key, so ParentKey and RootKey stay empty until the Phase 5 backfill.

- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Status_Acknowledged_Email, Send_Status_Progress_Email, Send_Status_ActionRequired_Email, Send_Status_Approved_Email, Send_Status_Declined_Email, Send_Status_Withdrawn_Email, Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. ### IP_SCAN_INTAKE

Source: docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/captures/IP_SCAN_INTAKE__5504d7f9-cc96-470c-be79-217582faf415.json (the tenant capture; this flow is not in the conformance package).

- §8.2: the year is no longer read in UTC and the LockToken is retired. Compose_Scan_Year and Compose_Scan_LockToken are removed; the kit's claim takes the WAT year.
- G-04, owner decision 2026-10-08: the trigger is open to anyone, as every other endpoint is, so the caller can no longer come from x-ms-client-principal-name (set only for a tenant-authenticated trigger; on an open one any caller could send it). The caller is the address of the sign-in proof Folio sends (core/scan-intake-service.js authHeaders), looked up in the proof ledger: unconsumed, Purpose internal-session, unexpired. A deposit always needs a valid proof: with none the caller is empty, no directory row matches, and the existing check answers 401. The directory and role check that follows is unchanged.
- §8.2: the Registry Reference is claimed by the generation kit (10 attempts, IF-MATCH, counter row found by Prefix and Year, floored at the highest number in Portal Registry), the same block SUBMISSION uses, so portal and scan share one number line (T2). The LockToken claim is removed. It also removes padLeft(), which the service refused live on 28 September ("The template function 'padLeft' is not defined or not valid"): every deposit that reached the number failed. When every attempt loses, the reply is 503 RETRY_LATER (was 409).
- S7 / §10.2: every scan now has a Portal Registry row, as every portal submission does: Title and ReferenceId = the reference, Subject = the file name, Channel scan, CorrespondenceType Incoming, Status received, AttachmentCount 1, AttachmentHashSet (first 12 hex of the declared SHA-256), EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, Direction In, CorrelationId and CreatedByRequest = the Request ID, and SourceLocator = the stored file's path. SenderEmail is the registry mailbox (Flow Configuration NOTIFY_REGISTRY_TO, else dgsRegistry@nitda.gov.ng), owner decision 4 October 2026: a paper letter's sender is not known to the system, so status e-mails for scans go to the registry. The scanning officer stays on the audit event. The row is written before the file, and if it fails a VOID row accounts for the number (Q2).
- §10.2 SCAN_LIBRARY: the stored file's library item gets its identity columns (EntityKey, whose first 8 hex are in the file name; ParentKey and RootKey REC:<the record's key>; RootRef; IdState ACTIVE; Rev 1; CreatedByRequest) through the kit's Guarded Update, addressed through Flow Configuration (DATASET_SCAN_LIBRARY_*). A failure here does not undo the deposit: the reply follows whatever its outcome.
- The reply now carries the fields Folio's scan service reads at its top level (core/scan-intake-service.js: referenceId, attachmentLink, stored, depositedBy, depositedAt, sha256, bytes). The flow answered with an envelope whose data held reference and resource, so even a successful deposit showed the officer an empty reference. The envelope keeps its own fields.
- §10.2 AUDIT_LOG: the deposit event in DGO_AuditLog carries its Entity Key, SubjectKey and RootKey REC:<key>, RootRef, CorrelationId, RevAfter 1, Process INTAKE and ContractKey SCAN_INTAKE.
- Two expressions carried over from the live flow are corrected. The notification condition tested contains(caller, "@") with a bare "@", which the workflow language reads as an empty expression, not the character; it is now "@@", the literal @. Compose_Complete_Run_Record wrapped its expression in @{...}, which makes the value text, so the final telemetry update's setProperty() on it failed on every run; it is now the object itself.
- §10.2 FLOW_TELEMETRY: the run row carries RequestId, CorrelationId (this flow starts the transaction), the Flow Registry Key DGO:<flow ID> and ContractKey SCAN_INTAKE.
- X-DGO-Size is read without failing when it is absent: the service evaluates both arms of if(), so int() of an empty header failed the scope before any check (a write-back carries no file). The value is chosen first and converted once: int(if(valid, the header, '0')); a deposit with no size still answers 400 from the size check.
- Tenant defect (8 October 2026, first live write-back): the caller's role is read from the directory row's Role choice, as FETCH_ALL reads it. The connector returns a Choice column as an object, which the flow read as text, so the RoleId lookup never matched and every caller was refused: 403 on a write-back, and no officer could deposit.
- Tenant defect (8 October 2026, first live write-back): an absent X-DGO-Filename failed the scope before any check, because substring() of an empty string fails ("start index must be less than the length") and a write-back carries no file. The decoded name is now empty when the header is: the name is padded with one character before it is cut and the pad is never part of the result. A deposit with no name still fails the metadata check.
- D1 / ITEM-6 (owner direction 2026-10-08, "proceed as recommended"): the staff status write-back is a second branch on the intake flow, which the owner identifies as IP_SCAN_INTAKE (ITEM-86). A request carrying X-DGO-Action: writeback sets a portal submission's status from Folio; every other request takes the deposit path unchanged. The caller is the sign-in proof's officer (above), who must be an active directory user (401) whose role carries "*" or the correspondence route (403). The body names referenceId, status (received, validation, review, action-required, approved or declined: the portal's governed values; withdrawn stays the citizen's) and optionally label and note (400 otherwise). The Portal Registry row is found by ReferenceId (404 if none) and gets Status, StatusLabel, ActionRequired, UpdatedAtUtc, AcknowledgedAtUtc on its first move past received, and ClosedAtUtc on approved or declined; a Portal Status Timeline row records the change with the officer as Actor. CG_Registry_Status_Notifier, triggered by the row change, tells the citizen.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_Scan_AuditFailed, Set_variable_varData_Scan_BadRequest, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Catch, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Denied_401, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Denied_403, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Deposited, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Duplicate, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Lock, Set_variable_varData_Scan_Oversize, Set_variable_varData_Scan_RateLimited, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_409, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_200, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_400, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_401, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_403, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_404, Set_variable_varStatusCode_Scan_Writeback_500.
- Administrative e-mail goes to the registry mailbox (owner decision, 2026-10-06): the fixed recipients Send_Telemetry_Email.To are set to dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng (the bulk-failure fallback was dgs@nitda.gov.ng). The configurable ones stay read from Flow Configuration (NOTIFY_OPS_TO, NOTIFY_REGISTRY_TO, NOTIFY_HELPDESK_TO), which fall back to the registry mailbox when blank.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_DGO_Scan_Notification_Email, Send_Telemetry_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

## Phase 3 tenant tests (§14.3)

Run once every Phase 3 flow is pasted (§13: Phase 3 exits on flow lint, which `npm run test:idphase3` is, and T1–T6):

| # | Test | Flow | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | 20 concurrent portal submissions | SUBMISSION | 20 distinct, consecutive NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN; no gaps; the counter equals the last |
| T2 | A portal submission and a scan intake in the same second | SUBMISSION, SCAN_INTAKE | Consecutive numbers from the one counter. Waits on SCAN_INTAKE (an internal flow, Phase 4 in this repo's sequence). |
| T3 | The same content twice within 24 hours | SUBMISSION | The second call returns the first reference; nothing new is issued |
| T4 | The client sends `requestId`, `ref` and `localId` | SUBMISSION, SUPPORT | Ignored; logged as ClientCorrelationId only |
| T5 | A support case naming a reference | SUPPORT | `^CASE-[A-HJ-NP-Z2-9]{6}$`; an ABOUT link when the record has an Entity Key |
| T6 | STATUS with NITDA-2026-217 (legacy) and with NITDA-2026-00217 | STATUS | Each resolves to its own record, or not found; never to the other |
